classification.difficultyReason: Reverse the area rule to recover a side, choose the cosine rule for the next side, then find an angle and check the appropriate inverse-sine branch using side sizes.

content.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$ shown opposite, the area of the triangle is $40\text{ cm}^2$. Find, correct to one decimal place:

spec.description: Unshaded triangle with C lower left, A above and B lower right; ordinary source blue outlines and labels rendered black in house style. The source prints the angle value without an arc.
spec.mathematics: CB = 14 cm; angle ABC = 42 degrees; area 40 square centimetres is supplied in the shared stem. No unknown lengths or angles are revealed.

answer.worked:
Let $x=\dfrac{80}{14\sin42^\circ}$, the unrounded value of $AB$. By the cosine rule:
$$\begin{align*}AC^2&=14^2+x^2-2\times14\times x\cos42^\circ\\AC&=\sqrt{14^2+x^2-28x\cos42^\circ}\\AC&\approx9.6\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$36.7^\circ$

Use the sine rule with the unrounded lengths.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ and $y$ be the unrounded values of $AB$ and $AC$. By the sine rule:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\angle ACB}{x}&=\frac{\sin42^\circ}{y}\\\sin\angle ACB&=\frac{x\sin42^\circ}{y}\\\angle ACB&=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{x\sin42^\circ}{y}\right)\\\angle ACB&\approx36.7^\circ\end{align*}$$
Since $AB<AC$, the opposite angle $\angle ACB<42^\circ$, so the acute solution is required.
